principles: Honor the fence's intent, don't game it: the allowlist must reflect the real, legitimate dependency boundary, never hide dependencies behind indirection.
Change tests and comments only; introduce zero shipping/runtime behavior change.
Keep the load-bearing security property (no finding-writer/advisory/gate import) independently enforced.
Bind every fix to a reproducible red->green transcript from a fresh build.
drivers: playbook.ts legitimately depends on two experience-layer helpers (source-lineage-audit, playbook-seed) the smoke allowlist never learned about.
learning-store.ts has a stricter fence and cannot absorb the helpers (they import dev-memory.js / playbook-runtime-memory.js).
The smoke is off the curated validate list, so the regression was silent and must be made green without masking a real breach.

options.name: Widen the fence allowlist
pros: Honestly reflects the real experience-layer/learning boundary
Touches no shipping code (helpers stay put)
The independent negative finding/advisory/gate assertion still guards the security property
cons: The positive allowlist grows by two entries
Requires refreshing the guardrail comment to stay truthful

options.name: Move helpers behind an allowed boundary (re-export via learning-store or a barrel module)
cons: learning-store's own stricter fence forbids it (helpers import dev-memory.js / playbook-runtime-memory.js)
A barrel indirection would hide the real dependency purely to satisfy a grep - fence-gaming, not fence-honoring
A larger, riskier refactor of shipping code for a test-only failure

rationale: Moving is infeasible cleanly because learning-store's stricter fence cannot absorb the helpers, and a barrel would only game the grep; widening the positive allowlist honestly reflects the legitimate experience-layer boundary while the independent negative assertion still guards the security property.

preMortem.scenario: Widening the allowlist silently permits a genuinely dangerous import later
preMortem.trigger: A future edit adds a finding-writer/advisory/gate import to playbook.ts
preMortem.consequence: The fence no longer catches a real boundary breach
preMortem.mitigation: The separate negative assertion !/finding.js$|advisory|gate/ remains and is exercised by CHK-001's adversarial intent; the non-vacuous planted-import check still proves the scanner detects a foreign import.

preMortem.scenario: The decision-doc assertion is 'fixed' by reintroducing retired wording instead of tracking the current contract
preMortem.trigger: Re-matching the old 'not remote receipt completion' string
preMortem.consequence: A stale test passes while masking real contract drift
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-002 binds the assertion to the CURRENT committed substring introduced by commit 8892270bf, verified by a green smoke run.

preMortem.scenario: The fix appears green only because of a stale worktree dist
preMortem.trigger: Running the smoke against an unrebuilt dist
preMortem.consequence: False green; main stays red after merge
preMortem.mitigation: Red and green are both captured from a fresh tsc build in the story worktree; red evidence pins baseline HEAD/material and the green run rebuilds first.

preMortem.scenario: The unrelated tier-c WIP on main is swept into this story's commit
preMortem.trigger: A broad git add in the worktree
preMortem.consequence: Foreign uncommitted work committed under the wrong story
preMortem.mitigation: Only the 3 scoped files are staged; excludedScope bars the tier-c docs; the worktree is isolated from main's working tree.
